mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals robust economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised upwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% and retail sales (RSAFS) increase by less than 0.5% in the same month, it signals a divergence between consumer spending and housing market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth concerns rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% & RSAFS increases < 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST declines and RSAFS weak increases on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
